newsitem.title: FRANCE: Casino names new management board head.
newsitem.headline: Casino names new management board head.

text.p: French retailer Groupe Casino said on Tuesday that the supervisory board had appointed Christian Couvreux to head the management board, replacing Georges Plassat.

Supervisory board chairman Jean-Charles Naouri, head of the Euris holding company, the leading shareholder in Casino, said in a statement: "The appointment of Christian Couvreux, previously a director, shows our willingness for continuity in management to ensure new profit growth."
Euris, through the Rallye company, controls a third of the capital and has 36.3 percent of the voting rights.

Board member Antoine Guichard, the representative of the Guichard family which holds 14.6 percent of the voting rights and 7.6 percent of the capital, was quoted in the Casino statement as saying he was in complete agreement with Naouri.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.

Couvreux, 46, joined Casino in 1990 and was appointed to the board last year. His appointment to the head of the management board comes amid big changes in the French food retail industry, which is consolidating to create bigger groups able to expand internationally.

Casino, which had 1996 sales of 77.35 billion francs, has long been rumoured as a potential merger mate to Promodes. Naouri said last month that he did not rule out a partnership between the two groups.
